results.title: Silky Crayons Review - Flanders Family Home Life
results.author: Jennifer Flanders
results.text:
Silky Crayons Review - Flanders Family Home Life

# Silky Crayons Review

Timberdoodle sent me a set of Silky Crayons to review this summer, and my grandkids love them. We’ve been using them for months!

The colors — twenty-four in all — are bright and vibrant. They provide great coverage, and will even show up on black paper.

The crayons themselves are virtually unbreakable. They never dry out and never need to be sharpened.

Best of all, the set is plenty big enough to share and has multiple shades of red, orange, yellow, green, blue, and purple, so nobody is forced to wait long for the color they need.

We took our Silky Crayons camping with us last week, and they helped keep my kids, grandkids, and even a few neighbors happily occupied while their parents visited around the campfire.

And just look at that smooth coverage! A red marker would have run out of ink before finishing that job. A red map pencil would not have been nearly so bright. And a regular red crayon would have likely broken in half long before the job was done.

The only caution I would give is that the pigments adhere better to normal paper with a matte finish. They tended to rub off a little when we used them on the slick poster-board craft project above.

But that never seemed to be a problem when we were using regular copy or construction paper or card stock.

Do you have a young artist who’d enjoy a set of Silky Crayons at your house? You can order your own through Timberdoodle as a stand-alone product or as part of their 2023 Preschool Curriculum Kit.

And while you’re on the Timberdoodle website, I’d encourage you to look around. We love everything we’ve ever ordered from this small family-owned company!

Be sure to sign up for their Doodle Dollar program to save on future purchases. And to see more of my Timberdoodle Reviews, simply scroll to the bottom of my Homeschool Help page, and you can read them all!

PLEASE NOTE: As a member of the Timberdoodle blog team, I routinely receive free or deeply discounted products in exchange for writing honest reviews. Opinions expressed in these posts are 100% my own. I’ve been a happy and enthusiastic Timberdoodle customer for decades — long before I ever started blogging for their company.

So this is the best choice for schools and parents; 🎨Wide uses - Dissolved in water, so this crayon is not just regualar crayons, it can also be used as a watercolor, oil painting and pastel, and it can also be used for face painting, so as long as there is Miya Himi crayons, whether in the art session, Toddlers, travels,home or participates in art party, you can enjoy artistic creation; 🎨Rotatable and erasable - Crayons use lipstick design, not only can rotate the same as lipstick, but also can be washable like lipstick, regardless of painted on the hands, clothes or on the desktop, the wall, so can be easily cleaned by water.

## Pricing & Reviews
Rated 4.7 from 30 reviews.
Top review: I bought this set for my grandson and we absolutely love the sleek smooth glide of the crayon. The colors are bright. We follow different instructional art classes on YouTube and it adds a perfect finishing touch to our masterpiece. I will definitely buy this again.The crayons do have a nice grip on them and feel nice to color with. They glide smoothly and are fairly easy to blend with.They're a little hard to be precise with in the beginning since it has a wide point. Also can't really erase it, but I expected this lol.Using it as watercolor is alright. The color seems fine but I just recently started using watercolors so I'm no expert by any means. (It's why I provided a picture)So in my opinion this would make a cute gift for any kid. The crayons are sturdy and won't break easily. And it's easy to carry around since they come with caps.I gave it 4 out of 5 stars because while the crayons themselves are nice....I would rather not use these as watercolor.Too waxy. Colors don't smudge into a smooth layer. Wouldn't buy them again. Attractively arranged.The Himi silkky crayons are a lot of fun. They are something in between a crayon and cary-pas and a watercolor pencil. I also tried Himi/ Miya watercolors and liked those much better than other nwer brands I had tried. Their watercolors do use pigment, rather than dye, like the vast majority of inexpensive watercolor paint. The crayons are almost certainly dye based. I did not get the breakup which you see with pigments in their crayons that I did with their watercolors. On the left is a little sample of their crayons. I actually tried to reproduce the doodle I did to test their watercolors. The crayons are on the left and watercolors on the right.The Silkky crayons did blend with water, but it too a lot of water, so much that it bled through (the green spots on the right are bleed through). I was able to smudge/ blend a bit when dry, and the water did smooth it out some, but not to the extent that you get with real watercolor paint.As a crayon it is a joy to use. It really does glide! There was not a sharpener included, though no doubt the could be brought to a point with a knife. That said, they are not precise like watercolor pencils, but like watercolor pencils, do leave a more definite line than you get with watercolor paint. They are waxy, but it is a soft wax, even softer than cray-pas.They are not much like Windson Newton watercolor crayons, which are from their pro line, and densely pigmented. Unfortunately, Windsor Newton has discontinued their crayons, and as far as I know, Himi is the closest available, though, again, the Windor Newton were pigment based and the Himi dye based. The Himi crayons are a lot less expensive, which also makes them easier to play with. That is, they are not so costly that I feel like I can only take them out when I am ready to do some serious work....which is great! It leaves a lot of room for experimentation.They are easy to use, twist out like a lipstick. Unfortunately there is not a huge amount of each color. The staick are around 1/2 inch long each. On the other hand, this is very inexpensive for a set of 36 colors, so replacing the set when one or more is used up is not too costly.Very little of what is on the package is in English, so I can not report on the content (pigment vs. dye e.g.). There are only 2 things in English on the package: 36 colors, and *Not suitable for use by children under 3 years old*. I am a bit confused because the description talks about use as face paint, and children's parties... I had the impression from the description that they were non-toxic, which is why I am puzzled about the warning for children under 3. (It also appears in a graphic on the box).If there is a representative here from Himi, could you please clarify? Why is there a warning that these are not suitable for use by those under 3?Ordered it as a present and got complemets about the colors and comfortability of use.My girl loves it because the color is so vivid, they make her drawings pop. It comes in 36 awesome colors. The crayons are creamy and glide smoothly. It's easy to use even for my toddler. The thick fat pens is easy for him to grip. It really help him to hold pen correctly. These also don't break as easily as the twistable Crayola we used to have. On the downside, they go through a lot each time they color so the set will probably not last long. They do have to wait for at least five minutes after they color. It's a bit wet and will leave marks everywhere if you don't let it dry. That said, they're easy to wash off the hands.My daughter loves these crayons. They are so easy to color with and their pigment is out of this world. They are easy to wipe off if you accidentally get them on the table . They feature a roll-up bottom to bring out more crayons. Way better than a box of crayons.
